data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word leirion, meaning lily. In Greek mythology, the lily was a symbol of purity and innocence. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. data.cultural_impact: The name "Lirio" holds a beautiful cultural significance in the Hispanic and Italian communities. It is derived from the Greek word "leirion," which means lily. In these cultures, the lily is a symbol of purity, beauty, and rebirth. Naming a child "Lirio" pays homage to this classical and revered meaning.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Lirio carries deep spiritual significance. The lily is regarded as a symbol of the resurrection, reminding us of Christ's victory over death. It is also a reflection of the spiritual purity and innocence sought after by followers of Christ. Additionally, the lily holds special significance as a symbol of the Virgin Mary, who embodies both purity and motherhood. Thus, the name "Lirio" may be given to a child as a reminder of the purity, innocence, and spiritual significance found in the Christian faith.
